\subsection{Where the hh self-energy enters the ch projection}
Reading the ledger \texttt{ledgers/P13\_ch\_dependency\_rows.json} (a computed control, not an assertion), the graphs
D01, D03 occur in exactly one row: $(S_0,\Gamma_1^{[2]})\,s_2\,K{:}K\!\cdot c$, with $\Gamma_1$ pattern $h^2$. The
same row also holds D02, D12 (zero, p15) and D11 (not evaluated). The slot functional is
\[
X_{hh}[c,h]=\int (s\,h)_{(mn)}(p;c)\;G^{(mn)(rs)}(p)\;h_{(rs)}(-p).
\]
The operator $s\,h$ is read off the $K\!\cdot c$ monomial of the frozen $S_\Psi^{(0)}$ (16 nonzero components). Its
covariant fit is exact and unique: $(s\,h)_{(mn)\nu}=\tfrac{i}{2}(\eta_{m\nu}p_n+\eta_{n\nu}p_m)$. It is therefore
LONGITUDINAL in $(mn)$.

\subsection{Decoupling (proof, exact in $d$)}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{H1.} $s\,h$ is longitudinal (above), so $X_{hh}$ depends on $G$ only through $p_mG^{(mn)(rs)}$. Because
$p\in$ QdS, $p\cdot\tilde g=0$, so $\tilde g$ on the pair $(mn)$ drops out.
\item \textbf{H2/H3.} $p_m\,(G_{D01}+G_{D03})^{(mn)(rs)}=0$ identically in $d$. This holds for the 4D part and for
the evanescent part separately: each of the six structures of $p_mG$ (for example
$\tilde g_{rs}p_n$: $-\tfrac{i\,p^4}{8(d-1)}$ from D01 and $+\tfrac{i\,p^4}{8(d-1)}$ from D03) cancels exactly. Hence
$X_{D01+D03}=0$ for all six external assignments (Q4S, QdS, mixed $\hat{}/\tilde{}$). With $D02=D12=0$, the hh slot
receives nothing from the evaluated graphs.
\item \textbf{H4 (controls).} $X_{D01}$ and $X_{D03}$ are each nonzero, and so are their evanescent parts alone. The
cancellation is therefore a property of the SUM (the ghost loop cancels the longitudinal part of the bubble), not of
each graph. The map is not trivially zero.
\item \textbf{Order.} At one loop the ch projection is linear in $\Gamma_1$, so no product of evanescent poles occurs.
The cancellation is exact in $d$ and not merely $O(\epsilon)$.
\end{itemize}
Mutations, each rejected (summed slot becomes nonzero): wrong relative sign of D03; D03 doubled (symmetry factor);
D03 with its evanescent part dropped (naive 4D); the trace operator $\eta_{mn}p_\nu$ in place of $s\,h$.

\emph{Verdict:} DECOUPLED (proof), as the sum D01 + D03 (+ D02 = D12 = 0), and not graph by graph. No evanescent
structure survives in the slot. No evanescent $h\cdot h$ counterterm is added, so the counterterm quotient is
unchanged and no contract file changes for this. The summed evanescent poles of the hh Green function are nonzero
(eight structures, recorded in the certificate) but transverse. Renormalizing the hh Green function itself would
need evanescent $h\cdot h$ counterterms; that matters only outside this projection and is not claimed. D11, in the
same row, is open.

\subsection{4D poles: coordinates and the transversality constraint}
The five p14r $h\cdot h$ directions span the five pair-symmetric 4-derivative 4D structures (rank 5), so span
membership is automatic. The sharper statement is a constraint. Longitudinality $p_mG^{(mn)(rs)}=0$ imposes rank-3
linear conditions on the coordinates $z$, which leaves a 2-dimensional transverse subspace with basis
$k_1=(\tfrac12,-\tfrac12,-1,1,0)$ and $k_2=(1,0,-2,0,1)$. The individual pole coordinates are not transverse:
\[
z_{D01}=i\,(-\tfrac{27}{160},-\tfrac{71}{240},\tfrac{19}{60},\tfrac{11}{20},-\tfrac{13}{30}),\qquad
z_{D03}=i\,(\tfrac{7}{96},\tfrac{1}{24},-\tfrac18,-\tfrac1{24},\tfrac1{12}).
\]
Their sum is transverse:
\[
z_{D01+D03}=i\,(-\tfrac{23}{240},-\tfrac{61}{240},\tfrac{23}{120},\tfrac{61}{120},-\tfrac{7}{20})
=i\,(\tfrac{61}{120}\,k_1-\tfrac{7}{20}\,k_2).
\]
This is the Ward-type statement the ch identity needs at this order. It is incomplete without D11.

\subsection{Phase convention (G6)}
Every graph is exported as $G=\kappa^2N_\epsilon\hat G$ with $N_\epsilon=iS_\epsilon/16\pi^2$. For D01 and D03,
$\hat G=-i\,\mathrm{pref}/\kappa^2\int$ with real export prefactors ($\kappa^2/2$, $-\kappa^2$), so $A(d)$ carries an
overall $i$. D13's exported prefactor is $i\kappa^2$, so its $A(d)$ is real. Because $s\,h=i(\dots)$, $X_{hh}$ is real
like the D13 slot. The D01/D03 relative phase is tested by H3 (mutation M1 breaks it). The D13-versus-hh relative
phase is not tested by a nonzero identity, since both slot contributions vanish. No physical overall phase is
asserted.

hazard of re-parsed strings (disclosed contract revision; no value affected). G1/G3: the guard docstring and the
disclosure now state exactly what is refused at runtime and what is excluded by the extended static AST scan:
